blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-security-1 (API tokens are stored in clear in the database) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-security-2 (The Authorization header, and so every token, is written to the logs) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
The `api_tokens` table holds `user_id`, `token` and `created_at`; the
middleware looks a request's token up with `WHERE token = $1`. Storing the
token as given keeps the lookup a simple indexed equality.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Tokens are stored as given
findings.recommendation: Anyone who reads the `api_tokens` table — a leaked backup or SQL dump, a read-only replica, a support account, an SQL injection elsewhere — gets every user's working bearer credential and calls the API as them (CWE-312 / CWE-256); since revocation is a Non-Goal, nothing can cut that access off. Store only a hash of the token (SHA-256 is enough for a 32-byte random value) in a `token_hash` column and look it up with `WHERE token_hash = $1`: the lookup stays a single indexed equality, so the stated reason for storing it as given does not hold. Update task 1.1 and 1.2 and the spec accordingly (the token is shown once and never stored).
findings.title: API tokens are stored in clear in the database

findings.evidence:
To diagnose integration problems, the middleware logs each request's
method, path and headers at `info` level, including `Authorization`, so
support can see which token an integration sent.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Every request is logged with its headers
findings.recommendation: Every request writes its bearer token (and, since all headers are logged, the `Cookie` session too — see `src/http/middleware.rs:21`) into the info logs; anyone with log access — support, a log aggregator, a shipped log archive — replays it and acts as the user until the token is revoked, which this change cannot do (CWE-532, CWE-200). Never log `Authorization` or `Cookie`: redact them (e.g. `Bearer ***`), and if support must identify a token, log a non-secret identifier such as the token's row id or a short prefix of its hash. Change task 1.3 so `logs_requests` asserts the redaction.
findings.title: The Authorization header, and so every token, is written to the logs
